routes.label: at a mission in the United States

note: The e-passport's fees and validity as the Prime Minister announced them at its launch, reported by iWitness News (5 March 2014): EC$150 for an adult and EC$80 for a minor in Kingstown, valid ten years over 16 and five years under 16. No later change was found (the Government's site answers 403 to this client), so the 2014 amounts stand. The missions' fees (CAD$145 and $75 in Canada, US$150 and $80 in the United States, £75 and £40 in the United Kingdom) are in other currencies: the abroad route carries the United States' (US$150 and US$80), the one abroad currency the form holds; Canada's and the United Kingdom's aren't held. Processing times are a lead.

sources.title: iWitness News, Vincentians to pay more for improved passport (5 March 2014)
sources.said: The e-passport will be valid for 10-years for persons older than 16 years old and for five years for persons younger than 16. ... An adult, who applies for a passport in Kingstown, will pay EC$150, while a minor will pay EC$80. Adult applicants in Canada will pay CAD$145, while a minor will pay CAD$75; in the United States, the fees will be US$150 and US$80, respectively, and in the United Kingdom, 75 pounds and 40 pounds, respectively. ...
